subject: chemistry
title: Conservation of mass
key_idea: No atoms are made or destroyed in a chemical reaction, so the total mass of the products equals the total mass of the reactants. A change in mass is only apparent: a gas has been taken in or has escaped, and its mass was not measured.

sections.heading: The law of conservation of mass

blocks.text: In a reaction, atoms are rearranged into new substances. This section covers what stays the same and how to show it.

items.meaning: The total mass of the products equals the total mass of the reactants. No atoms are lost or made.
A reaction where nothing can enter or leave, such as a sealed flask.
A reaction where a gas can enter or escape, such as an open flask or crucible.

items: The atoms in the products are the same atoms that were in the reactants.
That is why an equation must balance: each element has the same number of atoms on both sides.
In a **closed system** the total mass stays the same, even if a precipitate forms.

blocks.label: Mass is conserved
blocks.formula: total mass of reactants = total mass of products
where: Use the same unit on both sides, usually grams.

blocks.text: You can show the law with relative formula masses. The balanced equation WO₃ + 3H₂ → W + 3H₂O has Mr values WO₃ = 232, H₂ = 2, W = 184, H₂O = 18.

items.text: Both sides are 238, so mass is conserved.

items: No atoms are lost or made in a reaction.
Mass of reactants = mass of products.
In a sealed flask the total mass does not change.

blocks.text: In an open container the mass can go up or down. This section covers why, in terms of the particles.

rows: A gas from the air is a reactant and joins the solid. Its atoms are now part of the product.
Magnesium burns in air to make magnesium oxide.
A gas is a product and escapes. Its mass is no longer measured.
Zinc carbonate reacts with an acid and carbon dioxide leaves the flask.
A precipitate forms in a sealed flask.

items: Gas particles are far apart and move freely, so they escape from an open container.
The atoms still exist. They are in the gas, which is not weighed.
In thermal decomposition of a metal carbonate, carbon dioxide escapes and the metal oxide is the only solid left.

blocks.label: Mass of gas lost
where: Both masses are of the flask and its contents, in grams.
blocks.formula: mass of gas lost = mass before − mass after

diagram.alt: Practise calculating the mass of gas lost from the masses before and after a reaction.
working: Mass of gas lost = mass before − mass after
diagram.question: A flask and its contents have a mass of **{B} g** at the start of a reaction. After 8 minutes the mass is **{A} g**. A gas has escaped. Calculate the mass of gas lost.

items: Mass goes up if a gas joins the solid. It goes down if a gas escapes.
The atoms are not lost. The gas is simply not weighed.
Mass of gas lost = mass before − mass after.

sections.heading: Explaining a mass change in an exam

blocks.text: Mark schemes reward two ideas for a decrease in mass. Write both of them.

items: Name the gas that is produced, or say "a gas is produced".
Say that the gas **escapes** from the flask.
For an increase in mass, say that oxygen from the air has joined the solid.
Decrease: a gas is produced and it escapes.
Increase: a gas has been added to the solid.
Do not say atoms are lost or destroyed.

checks.q: State the law of conservation of mass.
checks.a: No atoms are lost or made in a chemical reaction, so the mass of the products equals the mass of the reactants.

checks.q: A student heats copper carbonate in an open test tube. The mass of the tube and contents goes down. Explain why.
checks.a: Carbon dioxide gas is produced. It escapes from the test tube, so its mass is no longer measured.

checks.q: Magnesium burns in air. The mass of the solid goes up. Explain why.
checks.a: Oxygen from the air joins the magnesium to make magnesium oxide, so the solid gains the mass of the oxygen.

worked_example.question:
A student adds a solution of ethanoic acid to zinc carbonate in an open flask on a balance.

Explain what happens to the mass of the flask and its contents during the reaction.
answer_points: The mass of the flask and contents decreases.
This is because carbon dioxide is produced.
The carbon dioxide escapes from the flask.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the decrease, one for naming carbon dioxide and one for the gas escaping.

worked_example.question:
The word equation for the reaction between magnesium and dilute hydrochloric acid is

magnesium + hydrochloric acid → magnesium chloride + hydrogen

A strip of magnesium ribbon was placed in the conical flask. 100 cm³ of dilute hydrochloric acid was added to the conical flask. The mass of the flask and contents was measured at regular intervals. The loss in mass was calculated.

Explain why there is a loss in mass of the flask and contents.
answer_points: The hydrogen escapes from the flask.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the gas formed and one for it escaping.

worked_example.question:
A student investigates the reaction between acids and metals.

Zn(s) + 2HNO₃(aq) → Zn(NO₃)₂(aq) + H₂(g)

The student investigates the reaction between zinc metal and nitric acid.

The student uses the balance to record the change in mass during the reaction.

The mass decreases. Explain why.
answer_points: Hydrogen is a gas, so a gas is produced.
The gas can escape from the beaker.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the gas and one mark for the idea that it escapes.
